name: Devel Debug Log
description: Stores debug information for an easier AJAX debugging.

suggests.drupal/devel: Some modules will be able to pretty-print PHP with this module.

consumes_plugin_types: devel_dumper (renders array/object messages via plugin.manager.devel_dumper, using the dumper chosen in devel.settings:devel_dumper — Kint by default)
provides_functions: ddl(mixed $message, string $title = '') — save one debug message to the devel_debug_log table
ddl_once(mixed $message, string $title = '') — save only if an identical message was not already stored this request (deduped by md5(serialize()))
provides_twig_functions: ddl(message, title) — Twig function; no-op unless twig.config:debug is TRUE
ecosystem_note: A tiny developer-only debugging aid, not an end-user feature. It adds an admin page at /admin/reports/debug (Reports > Debug messages, permission 'access debug messages', restrict access TRUE) that lists debug messages a developer explicitly stored by calling the global ddl()/ddl_once() PHP functions or the ddl() Twig function. Messages are appended as rows to a plain custom DB table (devel_debug_log: id, timestamp, title, message, serialized) — NOT a config or content entity, so nothing is exportable and there is no schema/config UI. Positioned as an alternative to drupal_set_message()/watchdog for cases (notably AJAX/subrequests) where on-page messages are awkward to read: the output persists on a dedicated page until you click 'Clear log messages'. Array/object messages are pretty-printed through Devel's dumper (Kint by default), which is why it hard-depends on devel:devel ^5.1 and serialization; the stored 'message' column already holds the rendered dumper markup (the raw value is not kept). The Twig ddl() function stays inert unless Twig debug is on. Ships no plugin types, services beyond a Twig extension, Drush commands, hooks, or config.
project_description:
Devel Debug Log is a developer module that provides a way for developers to save and display debug messages on a separate page in the web browser. It serves as an alternative to using drupal_set_message() or watchdog() for debugging, and a complementary module to Devel for those who find viewing messages in the browser easier than looking for them, say, in a file.

 The module provides the ddl($message) function, which the developer can use to save a debug message. If an object or array is supplied as $message, it will be displayed using the Krumo debugging tool. Messages can be viewed at Reports > Debug Messages.

 Dependencies 
 This module depends on Devel module.
